definitions.explanation: The prescribed sequence in which the strokes of a kanji or kana character should be written, considered important for proper form and legibility.

examples.japanese: {書|か}き{順|じゅん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{覚|おぼ}える→覚える：00739_oboeru⟧。
⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{漢字|かんじ}→漢字：09480_kanji⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{書|か}き{順|じゅん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{間違|まちが}え→間違える：01109_machigaeru⟧やすい。
examples.english: The stroke order of this kanji is easy to get wrong.

examples.japanese: ⟦{小学校|しょうがっこう}→小学校：01055_shougakkou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{書|か}き{順|じゅん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{正|ただ}しく⟦{習|なら}う→習う：00479_narau⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{大切|たいせつ}→大切：01456_taisetsu⟧だ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦されている→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: In elementary school, it is considered important to learn stroke order correctly.

notes:
The standard order in which strokes of a character are written. Japanese education places great emphasis on correct stroke order from elementary school, and it is tested in school exams. Following proper stroke order helps produce balanced, legible characters and builds muscle memory for faster writing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {書|か}き{順|じゅん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{覚|おぼ}える→覚える：00739_oboeru⟧: to memorize stroke order
- {書|か}き{順|じゅん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{違|ちが}う→違う：01957_chigau⟧: the stroke order is wrong
- ⟦{正|ただ}しい→正しい：00893_tadashii⟧{書|か}き{順|じゅん}: correct stroke order
- {書|か}き{順|じゅん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{確認|かくにん}する→確認する：25332_kakuninsuru⟧: to check the stroke order

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{筆順|ひつじゅん}→筆順：15242_hitsujun⟧: stroke order — a more formal synonym used in textbooks and dictionaries; same meaning
- ⟦{画数|かくすう}→画数：13581_kakusuu⟧: stroke count — the total number of strokes in a character, not the order
